summary: Font-agnostic forms for letters with two vowels. 1 Kgs 17:11, Ps 14:1 (two) and 53:2 (two): the ḥataf-ḥiriq in plus notation, the sheva's copy first, with the packed form after it in parentheses. Prov 6:24: the segol on an alef in double guillemets after the lamed's qamats, with qamats-CGJ-segol after it in parentheses. 2 Kgs 4:7: the qubuts before the bet, on an alef in double guillemets, without the CGJ

Proverbs.comment: Proverbs 6:24: the note's א?! form of לשון, whose lamed had a segol and a qamats; give the lamed its qamats and the segol to an alef in double guillemets after it, then, in parentheses, the lamed with qamats, CGJ and segol (option 3 of MAM-basics issue 332)

1Kings.comment: 1 Kings 17:11: the note's א form, of לקחי־נא, whose ḥataf-ḥiriq is a sheva then a ḥiriq on one letter; give it in plus notation, the letter with its sheva, then the letter with its ḥiriq, followed by the unchanged form in parentheses

Psalms.comment: Psalms 14:1: the note's first א form, of השחיתו, whose ḥataf-ḥiriq is a sheva then a ḥiriq on one letter; give it in plus notation, the letter with its sheva, then the letter with its ḥiriq, followed by the unchanged form in parentheses

Psalms 14:1: the note's second א form, of התעיבו, whose ḥataf-ḥiriq is a sheva then a ḥiriq on one letter; give it in plus notation, the letter with its sheva, then the letter with its ḥiriq, followed by the unchanged form in parentheses

Psalms 53:2: the note's first א form, of השחיתו, whose ḥataf-ḥiriq is a sheva then a ḥiriq on one letter; give it in plus notation, the letter with its sheva, then the letter with its ḥiriq, followed by the unchanged form in parentheses; the note's later prose quotation of the form stays as it is

Psalms 53:2: the note's second א form, of והתעיבו, whose ḥataf-ḥiriq is a sheva then a ḥiriq on one letter; give it in plus notation, the letter with its sheva, then the letter with its ḥiriq, followed by the unchanged form in parentheses

2Kings.comment: 2 Kings 4:7: the note's א-כתיב form of בניכי, whose bet had a qubuts, a CGJ and a qamats; the qubuts, which the note puts before the bet, moves to an alef in double guillemets before it, and the CGJ goes (MAM-basics issue 333)
